sources.citation: Santiago, Paul Julian. 2010. The Phonetic Structures of Kalanguya. B.A./M.A. thesis, University of the Philippines, Diliman (11 pp. in the academia.edu version; Glottolog says 31 pp.).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Treats stressed vs unstressed syllables as given (word list has two tokens per vowel in stressed and two in unstressed syllables) and finds no F1/F2 effect of stress on any of the four vowels ('the acoustic correlates of stress do not have any effect on Kalanguya vowel space'); recommends future work on 'acoustic correlates of stress and other prosodic features'. Says NOTHING about where stress falls or whether it is contrastive. Sec. 1.2 covers only the consonant/vowel inventory and orthography.
